overview.summary: Attention is a limited, consumable resource that directly impacts learning, memory, and engagement. Understanding attention mechanics is fundamental to designing effective educational experiences.
overview.keyInsight: Learning and memory are direct consequences of attentional processing: the more attention is directed toward something, the more likely it is to be learned and remembered.

resourcePoolModel.title: Attention as a Resource Pool
resourcePoolModel.description: Your attention is a finite resource that gets spent and consumed throughout the day, but can be rebuilt through intentional practices.

factors.effect: Provides short-term boost but depletes overall pool
Quick energy spike followed by attention crash
Chips away at attention without conscious awareness
Context switching rapidly drains attention reserves
Essential for attention restoration and memory consolidation
Time in nature reduces mental fatigue

moodConnection.title: Mood Affects Attention
moodConnection.description: Your emotional state directly impacts your ability to focus. Excitement and purpose significantly increase attention capacity.

principles.description: Whether or not you're excited to pursue something plays a significant role in how much attention you can dedicate to it
Goals provide purpose, contribute to positive emotions, and motivate action—leading to accomplishment and satisfaction
Personal interest in a subject can multiply available attention resources

learningConnection.title: Attention in Learning
learningConnection.keyFinding: Learning and memory are direct consequences of attentional processing: the more attention is directed or devoted toward something, the more likely it is that it will be later learned and remembered.
implications: Design learning experiences that capture and maintain attention
Use gamification to increase emotional investment in content
Break complex topics into attention-sized chunks
Provide variety to prevent attention fatigue
Connect new learning to existing interests
learningConnection.expanseApplication: Expanse uses gamification, rewards, and visual progress to increase emotional investment in learning, thereby increasing attention and improving retention.

practicalTakeaways.title: Mastery Through Practice
practicalTakeaways.description: True mastery of focus, attention, and mood comes through purposeful implementation, consistent practice, and improved understanding of how we learn.

techniques.description: Create mental pictures of what you're trying to learn
Connect new information to existing knowledge
See concepts from multiple angles to strengthen understanding
Focused, intentional practice rather than passive exposure

overview.summary: Effective feedback is a cornerstone of learning, particularly valuable when students make errors or demonstrate gaps in understanding.
overview.keyInsight: Feedback achieves great results especially when students make errors or demonstrate a lack of understanding, presenting an opportunity for deeper learning and positive growth.

roleInLearning.title: Feedback in Learning
roleInLearning.description: Learning involves feedback, which can include reinforcement (such as rewards) or criticism and corrective action. Feedback helps ensure learners continue to focus on content and make progress.

types.example: Rewards, praise, recognition for good work
Specific suggestions for how to improve
Visual progress bars, level-ups, achievement unlocks

errorOpportunity.title: Errors as Learning Opportunities
errorOpportunity.description: When students make errors, it presents a crucial opportunity for deeper learning and positive growth through targeted feedback.
principles: Frame errors as natural part of learning process
Provide specific, actionable guidance for improvement
Celebrate the attempt, not just the result
Use errors to identify knowledge gaps
Build resilience through constructive error handling

expanseApproach.title: Expanse Feedback Philosophy
principles: Immediate feedback on actions and progress
Personalized feedback based on individual progress

overview.summary: Positive reinforcement plays a significant role in learning by encouraging students to repeat good behaviors, build confidence, strengthen bonds, and develop positive motivation for success.

benefits.description: Positive reinforcement helps students associate good memories with their past choices, making them more likely to repeat those choices.
benefits.mechanism: Memory association between action and positive outcome

benefits.description: Positive reinforcement helps students feel more confident, leading to increased academic growth. This confidence encourages students to take risks, such as trying more difficult problems or exploring new topics.
Positive reinforcement helps students develop a positive motivation for success, as opposed to the fear of failure that negative reinforcement can spark.
benefits.mechanism: Intrinsic motivation cultivation vs. avoidance motivation

benefits.description: Positive reinforcement helps create stronger bonds between teachers and students.
benefits.mechanism: Trust and relationship building through recognition

benefits.description: Positive reinforcement helps students feel encouraged to make choices that lead to favorable outcomes.

positive.effect: Students pursue goals because they want to achieve

expanseImplementation.title: How Expanse Uses Positive Reinforcement
methods: Customizable rewards that matter to individual students
Immediate positive feedback on good choices

overview.summary: True mastery requires understanding foundations, not just using finished products. Unlearning and relearning builds adaptability and the ability to create custom solutions.
overview.keyQuestion: If one only ever knows the final product, do they fully comprehend and appreciate the ingredients and purpose of the solution?

offTheShelfProblem.title: The Problem with 'Off the Shelf' Solutions
offTheShelfProblem.description: Using only finished products without understanding their foundations limits true comprehension and adaptability.

foodAnalogy.example: Consider premade foods, like microwavable chicken. If we only consume it without preparing it ourselves, do we truly understand its ingredients and the rationale behind its preparation?
foodAnalogy.lesson: Understanding the core ingredients and their individual contributions enables customization and optimization

softwareAnalogy.example: If we only know frameworks or turn designs into code, do we really understand the design or the problems the framework is solving?
softwareAnalogy.lesson: Deep understanding of fundamentals enables better solutions and adaptability

understandingCore.title: Understanding the Core
understandingCore.description: To fully appreciate any solution, break it down into core ingredients and understand each component's purpose.

questions: How does the chicken taste by itself?
What does adding breading do without oil?
What's the purpose of the oil?
chickenExample.outcome: By understanding each ingredient and its impact, we can create custom solutions optimized for specific needs

benefits.description: Adjust to feedback and personal preferences
Expand upon foundations to create unique solutions
Understand the full picture to address root causes
Explain concepts at multiple levels of abstraction

keyQuestion.question: Are you limited to one dish, or do you possess a broad range of skills ready for a global audience?

overview.summary: Visible progress is a powerful motivator. Our brains are wired to seek completion and advancement, making progress tracking an essential component of sustained engagement.

progressPrinciples.description: Progress must be visible to be motivating
progressPrinciples.implementation: Progress bars, level indicators, achievement displays

progressPrinciples.description: Progress relative to goals and peers provides context
progressPrinciples.implementation: Leaderboards, personal bests, goal completion rates

overview.summary: Our brains love repeating activities that reward us. By using reward systems strategically, we can train ourselves to choose better habits by making them more rewarding.

brainAndRewards.title: How the Brain Responds to Rewards
brainAndRewards.description: Our brains are wired to repeat activities that provide rewards. This fundamental mechanism can be leveraged to build positive habits.
brainAndRewards.insight: Homework or daily work might not feel as rewarding as watching TV or buying new items. But what if we could tip the scales in our favor?

habitFormation.title: Reward-Based Habit Formation
habitFormation.description: By associating rewards with desired behaviors, we can make those behaviors more appealing and likely to be repeated.

technique.step1: Identify the behavior you want to make a habit
technique.step4: Notice the increased motivation when you associate rewards with tasks
technique.result: Over time, the behavior becomes intrinsically rewarding

practicalExamples.reward: Treat yourself to something you enjoy
practicalExamples.outcome: Content creation becomes associated with positive feelings

expanseApproach.title: How Expanse Leverages Reward Psychology
methods: Variable reward schedules for sustained engagement
Personalized rewards that matter to individual students
Social rewards through recognition and leaderboards

overview.summary: The difference in output between a group of people who show up to do a job and a group of people who show up to accomplish a mission is nearly unfathomable.

jobVsMission.title: Job Mentality vs. Mission Mentality
jobVsMission.implication: Helping students find purpose and mission in their education dramatically increases engagement and outcomes

expansePurpose.title: Expanse Mission Connection
approach: Connect daily tasks to larger goals and meaning
Help students visualize their future success
Make the invisible benefits of education visible

coreBeliefs.title: Content Quality & Level Matching
coreBeliefs.insight: The quality of content and whether it's at the student's level is a major factor in engagement
coreBeliefs.application: Advertising piece for Expanse EDU - personalized, level-appropriate content drives engagement

coreBeliefs.title: Value of Human Performance
coreBeliefs.insight: Even if AI can do it better than humans, we still like watching humans do things and compete. Gaming proves this - AI bots are already way better than humans could be but people still prefer watching actual humans.
coreBeliefs.application: Balance AI assistance with human achievement celebration

coreBeliefs.title: Future of Human AI Interaction
coreBeliefs.insight: Future is games, entertainment, observability, teaching, customization, personalization, and engagement. Teaching students to understand what it means to be human helps them adapt, improve mental health, and prepare for jobs.
coreBeliefs.application: Core product direction and messaging - the human AI overall

coreBeliefs.title: Standardized Testing Paradox
coreBeliefs.insight: People criticize AI for being judged based on standardized tests, yet this is exactly what humans are trained on.
coreBeliefs.application: Opportunity for alternative assessment methods that measure true understanding

coreBeliefs.title: IQ/EQ Over Memorization
coreBeliefs.insight: Improving general IQ, ability to understand and operate within reality, and the human AI may be higher value than memorizing information. Improving emotional intelligence and communication are highly valuable.
coreBeliefs.application: Design features that develop reasoning, emotional intelligence, and soft skills

coreBeliefs.title: AI as Information Bridge
coreBeliefs.insight: AI improves flow of information to humans and improves information flow from human to human, as does improved education.
coreBeliefs.application: Position AI as communication enabler, not replacement

coreBeliefs.title: Question-Asking Culture Barrier
coreBeliefs.insight: Students don't feel like they should ask questions. In China/Eastern culture they may feel they're imposing on teacher's time. Asking questions is one of the best times for learning - we are primed to learn in this regard.
coreBeliefs.application: Create safe spaces for questions, normalize inquiry, anonymous question options

coreBeliefs.title: Missing Purpose & Value Understanding
coreBeliefs.insight: Students haven't yet learned the value of their education. They are missing purpose and understanding of the need for income to pay rent, get food, and how education translates into a better future. Also relating information to what they are interested in.
coreBeliefs.application: Connect learning to real-world outcomes and personal interests

coreBeliefs.title: Educational Software Gap
coreBeliefs.insight: Outdated technology and poor quality educational software. Need for better software. Opportunity for massively improved learning and better experiences. China is very behind in some areas of software development (but so is a lot of the world).
coreBeliefs.application: Market positioning and expansion opportunity - superior software experience

coreBeliefs.title: Universal Innovation Potential
coreBeliefs.insight: Every industry has the potential to be innovated.
coreBeliefs.application: Mindset for expansion and feature development - no limits

coreBeliefs.title: Regional Testing Content
coreBeliefs.learning: Politics is on tests in China
coreBeliefs.application: Consider regional curriculum requirements when expanding internationally

insights.title: Music & Binaural Beats
insights.insight: Music alignment with binaural beats and mind-body connection is highly important for focus.
insights.application: Consider audio/music features for focus enhancement, study playlists

insights.title: Diet & Allergen Impact on Focus
insights.insight: Healthy diet and avoiding allergens dramatically impacts our ability to focus and produce high quality work. Examples: dairy allergies, sugar excess, wheat/gluten allergies, pet dander exposure.
insights.application: Potential health/nutrition tracking features, educational content about focus and diet
